name: Next.js
one_liner: The dominant React application framework, and the main vehicle for server components.
what_it_is: A React framework providing file-based routing, server rendering, static generation and API routes. Its App Router is built around React server components and streaming.
why_it_matters: Next.js is where most React teams end up, and it is the place where the server-components shift is actually encountered. It also carries a real critique worth knowing: its rendering model is genuinely complicated, and its tightest deployment story points at one vendor. Both things are true at once.
suitable_for: React applications needing server rendering and routing without assembling them
Teams that want one framework covering both marketing pages and app
not_suitable_for: Simple content sites, where it is more machinery than required
Teams unwilling to track a fast-moving rendering model
Deployments with hard constraints that its serverless-shaped defaults fight against
